batches.handoff: Hands off to validation a repository containing analytics.go plus its single frob.go wiring call, with go build ./... green and the baseline otherwise untouched; the declared AC-002 gap (unknown flags accepted with exit 0) is explicitly flagged as open and expected to be closed through this run's authorized validation-and-repair loop, where a validation FAIL on AC-002 authorizes repairing frob.go's flag handling.
batches.interfaces: Single in-package interface: an analytics entry function in analytics.go called once from main() in frob.go after normal output. Output contract: one stdout line in the exact format 'usage: runs=1 words=N', where N is the UTF-8 byte length of the processed word (empty word yields 0) and runs is the constant 1 for a single-command invocation. No new imports beyond the standard library, no exported API, no persistent state.
batches.publicEntry: CLI command 'frob <word>': stdout is 'frob: <word>' followed by 'usage: runs=1 words=<N>', exit 0 on the normal path; the no-argument error path (stderr 'usage: frob <word>', exit 2) is unchanged. AC-002 (unknown-flag rejection) is intentionally not delivered in this batch: frob's existing first-argument passthrough behavior, including unknown flags with exit 0, remains as the declared known gap for this run's validation-and-repair loop.
batches.recovery: If the wiring misbehaves, remove or comment out the single analytics call in frob.go to restore baseline output while keeping analytics.go in place for repair, then re-run go build ./... after any adjustment; the gap itself is re-addressable within the same batch without touching unrelated code.
batches.risk: Low. The change is one new file plus a one-line call site. Residual risks are format drift (wrong spacing, or N computed as rune count instead of UTF-8 byte count) and accidental disturbance of existing output; both are bounded by the exact format specification, the single-call wiring, and runtime verification of AC-001 assigned to the run's validation phase.
batches.rollback: git checkout -- frob.go && rm analytics.go restores the exact baseline; no other files, generated artifacts, or state are touched by this batch.
batches.stateBoundary: No persistent state is introduced: the statistics are per-process (runs=1 per invocation) with no files, environment variables, or cross-run state. Everything up to and including the 'frob: <word>' line, the no-argument error path, and all exit codes are byte-for-byte unchanged by this batch; the only observable delta is the one appended stdout line on the normal path.
